details:
**Iblis refuses to bow**
In the Quran, God commanded the angels to bow down (prostrate) before Adam, and all obeyed except Iblis, who said he was better because he was made of smokeless fire while Adam was made of clay. For this pride Iblis was cast out of heaven and became Satan (Shaitan).

**Eve (Hawwa)**
Adam's wife, called Hawwa or Hawa in Islam. In Genesis, God creates her from one of Adam's ribs while he sleeps, after Adam has named the animals and found no suitable partner among them.

**Lilith**
In Jewish folklore, Adam's first wife, who refused to be subordinate to him and left Eden; some traditions say she joined or coupled with the demon Samael. She is often portrayed as a demon who threatens newborn children.

**Tree of Knowledge and the expulsion from Eden**
God forbade Adam and Eve to eat the fruit of the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, but the serpent (Iblis or Shaitan in the Quran) tempted them and they ate it. As a result they were expelled from the Garden of Eden (Jannah, or Paradise, in Islam).

**"Dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return"**
Part of God's curse on Adam in Genesis 3, along with the sentence that he will eat bread "in the sweat of thy face [brow]." Adam was formed from dust or clay (in the Quran by God's command "Be"), and his name is linked to the Hebrew adamah, "ground," and in Arabic tradition to a word for "skin" or the surface of the earth.

**Sixty cubits tall**
According to a hadith narrated by Abu Huraira, Muhammad said that God created Adam sixty cubits tall. The same tradition says that everyone who enters Paradise will have Adam's form and height.

**Forty years given to David (Dawud)**
In a hadith, Adam was shown his descendants and, seeing that David (Dawud) had a short life, gave him forty years from his own 1,000-year lifespan. When the angel of death came, Adam forgot or denied the gift, which is said to be why his descendants deny, forget, and make mistakes.

**First prophet of Islam (Safiullah)**
In Islam, Adam is regarded as the first prophet, bearing the honorific Safiullah, "the Chosen of God." Muslims consider him the first in the line of prophets that ends with Muhammad.

**Taught the names of all things**
In the Quran (Surah 2), God taught Adam the names of all things and then asked the angels to name them, which they could not do, showing Adam's superiority. In Genesis, Adam similarly gives names to all the animals.

**Cain and Abel**
Adam and Eve's first two sons. Cain murdered his brother Abel out of jealousy over God's acceptance of Abel's offering, and the Quran draws a lesson from the story that killing one person is like killing all of humanity.

**Seth**
Adam's third son (Sheth in Islamic tradition), born after Abel's murder as a replacement for him. In Islamic tradition, Adam named him his successor.

**Twin children**
Islamic tradition holds that Eve bore Adam many sets of twins (sometimes said to be 120 pairs), with each son marrying the twin sister of another son. In Shia tradition, Adam's first child was a single daughter named Anaq.

**Romans 5 and original sin**
In Romans 5, Paul calls Adam "a type of the one who was to come," presenting Christ as a new Adam whose obedience undoes Adam's disobedience. The fall of Adam and Eve is the basis of the Christian doctrine of original sin, developed especially by Augustine.

**Mount Arafat**
According to some Islamic traditions, Adam and Eve were separated after being sent down from Paradise and were finally reunited at Mount Arafat near Mecca, a central site of the Hajj.

**Sri Pada (Adam's Peak)**
A mountain in Sri Lanka with a large footprint-shaped rock at its summit. Muslims attribute the footprint to Adam, who is said to have first set foot on earth there, while Buddhists attribute it to the Buddha and Hindus to Shiva.
